newsitem.title: USA: ACLU sues N.Y. over computer indecency law.
newsitem.headline: ACLU sues N.Y. over computer indecency law.

text.p: The American Civil Liberties Union sued New York state Tuesday to block a state law that prohibits the dissemination of indecent materials over the Internet.

The ACLU alleged in the lawsuit filed in federal court in Manhattan that the New York law was an unconstitutional restriction of free speech that would reduce adult communications to levels acceptable for a 6-year-old.

"It is sad that the state of New York, known for its wide-ranging free speech traditions and dedication to the arts, has passed a law that could send a person to prison for up to four years for talking about safer sex or displaying online classic nudes or other artistic images," said Norman Siegel, executive director of the New York Civil Liberties Unon.
There are 14 other plaintiffs in the lawsuit, including the American Library Assocation, the Association of American Publishers and Magazine Publishers of America.
Named as defendants are New York Gov. George Pataki and state Attorney General Dennis Vacco.
The ACLU said the New York law was similar to the U.S. Communications Decency Act, which has been found to be unconstitutional by federal judicial panels in both Philadelphia and New York.
The U.S. Supreme Court has agreed to review findings by the Philadelphia panel but no date has been set for arguments.

The lawsuit filed Tuesday against the New York state law was the second challenge to a state censorship law relating to the Internet. The first was filed by the ACLU and others against a statute in Georgia. That case is expected to go to trial later this month.
The ACLU said it has been monitoring state regulation of the Internet and that more than 20 states have considered such laws.
